trigger: An update batch to a TRA is paused (TestInjection.directUpdateLatch, standing in for slow indexing) after its RoutedAliasUpdateProcessor was built with router.interval=+1DAY; meanwhile an admin runs ALIASPROP router.interval=+1HOUR, and then the batch's next document needs a new collection.
reason: The triggers (a delayed request and a concurrent, documented ALIASPROP change) are realistic. RAUP keeps the TRA configuration it read at request start, although aliases.adoc:119-121 says it checks for property changes per document, so it asks MAINTAINROUTEDALIAS for myalias__TRA__2017-10-24. The Overseer rebuilds the TRA from the current props (MaintainRoutedAliasCmd.java:116) and calcAdd creates 'the next one' under the new interval (TimeRoutedAlias.java:601-603, whose own comment says it 'may or may not be the same as our target'). It returns success, and doSynchronous then bails with SERVER_ERROR because its stale target is absent (RoutedAlias.java:348-351) instead of recomputing the candidate as the surrounding loop is built to do. The whole valid batch is rejected with a 500. A client retry with a fresh processor should succeed, and the extra collection is legitimate under the new interval, so the impact is limited.
summary: A routed-alias update does not refresh TRA properties during a request (contrary to the ref guide), so a concurrent ALIASPROP router.interval change makes the Overseer create a different collection and the batch fails with 'After we attempted to create X it did not exist'.
